title: Making plans with friends
goal: Ask a friend if they're free, suggest what to do, agree where and when to meet, say you're on your way or running late, and cancel without upsetting anyone.
intro:
Welcome to **Part 2**. From here on the course is about real life: the Hindi you need with friends, around town and at work. This unit is about making plans, which in Hindi means a lot of **चलो** 'let's', a lot of English words (**फ़्री**, **बिज़ी**, **प्लान**, **वीकेंड**) and the famous **बस पाँच मिनट!** 'just five minutes!'

You'll learn the everyday way to say 'let's' (**चलो, पिक्चर देखते हैं**), how to ask 'shall we?' (**कहाँ मिलें?**), how to boss your friends around (**टाइम पर आना!**), and how to say you're about to leave, on your way, or stuck in traffic.

grammar.title: Let's… and shall we…?
grammar.body:
Hindi has three everyday ways to suggest doing something together.

**1. चलो + present habitual (-ते हैं)** — the most common in speech: **चलो, पिक्चर देखते हैं** 'let's watch a film', **कल मिलते हैं** 'let's meet tomorrow / see you tomorrow'. It literally says 'we watch', but with चलो (or just the context) it is a suggestion. **चलो, चलते हैं** means 'right, let's go' or 'I'll be off then'.

**2. चलो + subjunctive (-एँ)** — a little more careful: **चलो, कुछ खाएँ** 'let's eat something'.

**3. Shall we? = the subjunctive as a question**: **चलें?** 'shall we go?', **कहाँ मिलें?** 'where shall we meet?', **क्या करें?** 'what shall we do?'. To suggest an idea: **क्यों न** + subjunctive: **क्यों न हम घर पर ही खाएँ?** 'why don't we just eat at home?'

With people you call आप, use **चलिए** instead of चलो.

The trap: the future is not a suggestion. **हम कल मिलेंगे** states a plan ('we will meet tomorrow'); to propose it, say **कल मिलते हैं** or **कल मिलें?**

examples.en: Let's meet tomorrow. / See you tomorrow.

examples.native: क्यों न हम इस बार घर पर ही पार्टी करें?
examples.roman: kyoṃ na ham is bār ghar par hī pārṭī kareṃ?
examples.en: Why don't we have the party at home this time?
Right, let's go. / I'll be off now. (polite)

grammar.title: Telling friends what to do: आओ, आ, आना
grammar.body:
You met the imperative in unit 11. With friends you will use three forms all the time:

**तुम-form: stem + ओ** — आओ, बताओ, चलो, करो. Your default with friends.
**तू-form: bare stem** — आ, बता, चल, कर. Only with your closest friends (or younger siblings); with anyone else it sounds rude.
**The -ना form (the infinitive)** — आना, बताना, भूलना. Used for instructions about **later**, and it sounds a bit softer: **कल टाइम पर आना** 'be on time tomorrow', **घर पहुँचकर मैसेज करना** 'text when you get home'.

**Negative**: put **मत** before the verb: **लेट मत होना** 'don't be late', **भूलना मत** 'don't forget' (मत can also follow the -ना form).

**Softening**: add **ना** at the end to coax (**चलो ना!** 'oh come on, let's go!', **बताओ ना!** 'go on, tell me!'), or use a compound verb: **आ जाओ** 'come on over' feels friendlier than a bare आओ.

When your friend's parents are there, switch back: **आइए**, **बताइए**, **चलिए**.

The trap: the ना at the end is not 'no'. चलो ना means 'please come', and मत is the word for 'don't'.

examples.native: जल्दी आओ, सब आ गए हैं।
examples.roman: jaldī āo, sab ā gaye haiṃ.

examples.en: Come on, hurry up! (to a best friend)

examples.native: रात को मैसेज करना, भूलना मत।
examples.roman: rāt ko maisej karnā, bhūlnā mat.

examples.en: Come on, tell me what happened!
Uncle, please come in. (switching to polite)

grammar.title: About to leave, on the way, already there
grammar.body:
Being late is a national sport, so Hindi has precise ways to say where you are in the process:

**About to**: verb + **-ने वाला / वाली / वाले** + हूँ/है (from unit 13): **मैं निकलने वाला हूँ** 'I'm about to leave'.
**Right now / on the way**: the present continuous — **मैं आ रहा हूँ** 'I'm coming', **बस पहुँच रही हूँ** 'just arriving' — or **रास्ते में हूँ** 'I'm on the way'.
**Already done**: stem + **गया / गई** (+ हूँ): **मैं निकल गया हूँ** 'I've left', **मैं पहुँच गई** 'I'm here'. The compound with जाना marks the change as complete.
**Promising**: **मैं आता हूँ** (present habitual) means 'I'm coming / I'll be right there': रुको, मैं आता हूँ.

Everything agrees with the speaker: a woman says निकलने **वाली** हूँ, निकल **गई** हूँ, आ **रही** हूँ.

The trap: **मैं निकला** on its own sounds like a story ('I left'); for 'I've left (and I'm coming)' say **निकल गया हूँ**.

examples.native: हम खाना खाने वाले हैं, तुम भी आ जाओ।
examples.roman: ham khānā khāne vāle haiṃ, tum bhī ā jāo.
examples.en: We're about to eat, come and join us.

examples.native: मैं घर से निकल गया हूँ।
examples.roman: maiṃ ghar se nikal gayā hūṃ.

examples.native: वो रास्ते में है, बस पहुँच रही है।
examples.roman: vo rāste meṃ hai, bas pahuṃch rahī hai.
examples.en: She's on her way, almost there.

dialogue.title: Saturday film plan
dialogue.setting: Delhi. Friday lunch break: Sneha and Rohan, colleagues and friends, plan the weekend. Then Saturday evening, on the phone.

lines.speaker: Rohan

lines.speaker: Sneha

lines.roman: shām kā sho, sāt baje. Sāket vāle mol meṃ.
lines.en: The evening show, at seven. At the mall in Saket.

lines.speaker: Sneha
lines.native: मेट्रो स्टेशन के बाहर, साढ़े छह बजे। और लेट मत होना!
lines.roman: meṭro sṭeshan ke bāhar, sāṛhe chhah baje. aur leṭ mat honā!
lines.en: Outside the metro station, half past six. And don't be late!

lines.speaker: Sneha
lines.native: रोहन, कहाँ हो? मैं बीस मिनट से वेट कर रही हूँ!
lines.roman: rohan, kahāṃ ho? maiṃ bīs minaṭ se veṭ kar rahī hūṃ!
lines.en: (Saturday, 6:50 pm) Rohan, where are you? I've been waiting twenty minutes!

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.native: सॉरी, सॉरी! मैं रास्ते में हूँ, ट्रैफ़िक में फँस गया हूँ। बस पाँच मिनट!
lines.roman: sorī, sorī! maiṃ rāste meṃ hūṃ, ṭraifik meṃ phaṃs gayā hūṃ. bas pāṃch minaṭ!
lines.en: Sorry, sorry! I'm on my way, I got stuck in traffic. Just five minutes!

lines.speaker: Sneha
lines.native: तुम्हारे पाँच मिनट मुझे पता हैं। मैं टिकट ले रही हूँ, तुम सीधे अंदर आ जाना।
lines.roman: tumhāre pāṃch minaṭ mujhe patā haiṃ. maiṃ ṭikaṭ le rahī hūṃ, tum sīdhe andar ā jānā.
lines.en: I know your five minutes. I'm getting the tickets, you come straight in.

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.native: पक्का! और पॉपकॉर्न मेरी तरफ़ से!
lines.roman: pakkā! aur popkorn merī taraf se!
lines.en: Promise! And the popcorn's on me!

culture: Plans among friends in north India are loose and made late: 'tonight?' at 5 pm is normal, and the group chat decides more than any one person. Time is stretchy: **बस पाँच मिनट** and **मैं निकल गया हूँ** are often said by someone still at home, and nobody is shocked by 20 minutes' delay (offices and trains are another matter). A flat **नहीं** to an invitation sounds harsh, so people soften it: **देखते हैं** 'we'll see', **कोशिश करूँगा** 'I'll try', **सॉरी यार, आज नहीं हो पाएगा** — all of which may mean no. If you organise the outing, people may expect you to pay, and whoever suggested food often says **मेरी तरफ़ से** 'it's on me'. With friends you use **तुम** (and **तू** with very close ones), but if a friend's parent picks up the phone or opens the door, switch instantly to **आप**, **जी** and **आइए**.

lessons.title: Asking if a friend is free

tip.title: With friends: तुम, and English words with Hindi grammar
tip.body:
- With friends use **तुम** → **हो**: फ़्री **हो**? (best friends: तू → **है**).
- A rising voice makes the question; no क्या needed.
- English words slot right in and take Hindi grammar: **प्लान** बनाना, **टाइम** है?, **बिज़ी** हूँ.
- To a friend's parent: back to **आप … हैं**.

tip.title: Let's: चलो, … -ते हैं
tip.body:
- The everyday 'let's': **चलो, … -ते हैं**: चलो, पिक्चर देखते हैं.
- A bit more careful: **चलो + -एँ** (subjunctive): चलो, कुछ खाएँ.
- 'Shall we?' is the subjunctive as a question: **चलें?** **लंच करें?**
- Not the future: हम मिलेंगे = 'we will meet', not 'let's meet'.

sentences.en: Let's have dinner out tonight.

tip.title: Telling friends what to do
tip.body:
- **तुम**: stem + **ओ**: आओ, बताओ. Best friends (**तू**): bare stem: आ, बता, चल.
- For later, use the **-ना** form: टाइम पर **आना** 'be on time', **भूलना मत** 'don't forget'.
- **मत** = don't: लेट **मत** होना.
- Soften with **ना** at the end (चलो **ना**! 'oh come on!') or a compound: **आ जाओ**.

sentences.en: Don't be late, the film starts at seven.

lessons.title: I'm on my way!

tip.title: About to leave → on the way → there
tip.body:
- About to: **-ने वाला हूँ**: मैं निकलने वाला हूँ.
- On the way: **रास्ते में हूँ**, or the continuous: **आ रहा हूँ** 'I'm coming'.
- Already done: stem + **गया / गई**: मैं निकल **गया** हूँ 'I've left', पहुँच **गया** 'I'm here'.
- Women: निकलने **वाली** हूँ, निकल **गई** हूँ, आ **रही** हूँ.
tip.pattern: निकलने वाला हूँ → निकल गया हूँ → पहुँच गया

new: मैं ट्रैफ़िक में फँस गया हूँ।

sentences.native: मैं बस निकलने वाला हूँ।
sentences.roman: maiṃ bas nikalne vālā hūṃ.
sentences.en: I'm just about to leave. (man speaking)

sentences.native: मैं निकल गई हूँ, बीस मिनट में पहुँचूँगी।
sentences.roman: maiṃ nikal gaī hūṃ, bīs minaṭ meṃ pahuṃchūṃgī.
sentences.en: I've left, I'll be there in twenty minutes. (woman speaking)

sentences.native: तुम कहाँ हो? मैं कब से वेट कर रहा हूँ।
sentences.roman: tum kahāṃ ho? maiṃ kab se veṭ kar rahā hūṃ.
sentences.en: Where are you? I've been waiting for ages. (man speaking)

sentences.native: सॉरी, ट्रैफ़िक बहुत है, मैं थोड़ा लेट हो जाऊँगा।
sentences.roman: sorī, ṭraifik bahut hai, maiṃ thoṛā leṭ ho jāūṃgā.
sentences.en: Sorry, there's a lot of traffic, I'll be a bit late.

sentences.native: वो ट्रैफ़िक में फँसी है।
sentences.roman: vo ṭraifik meṃ phaṃsī hai.
sentences.en: She's stuck in traffic.

sentences.native: मैं पहुँच रहा हूँ, बस दो मिनट!
sentences.roman: maiṃ pahuṃch rahā hūṃ, bas do minaṭ!
sentences.en: I'm nearly there, just two minutes!

sentences.native: तुम निकले या नहीं?
sentences.roman: tum nikle yā nahīṃ?
sentences.en: Have you left or not?

sentences.native: मैं पहुँच गया, तुम कहाँ हो?
sentences.roman: maiṃ pahuṃch gayā, tum kahāṃ ho?
sentences.en: I'm here, where are you? (man speaking)

sentences.native: वेट करो, मैं रास्ते में हूँ।
sentences.roman: veṭ karo, maiṃ rāste meṃ hūṃ.
sentences.en: Wait, I'm on my way.

lessons.title: Cancelling without upsetting anyone

tip.title: Saying no without saying no
tip.body:
- A flat नहीं sounds harsh. Soften it: **सॉरी यार, आज नहीं हो पाएगा** 'sorry, I won't manage today'.
- Offer another time: **कोई और दिन?**, or push it back with **टालना**.
- **देखते हैं** 'we'll see' often means no.
- **कैंसल करना** = you cancel it; **कैंसल होना** = it gets cancelled.

new: सॉरी यार, आज नहीं हो पाएगा।

sentences.native: सॉरी यार, आज नहीं हो पाएगा, कल पक्का।
sentences.roman: sorī yār, āj nahīṃ ho pāyegā, kal pakkā.
sentences.en: Sorry man, can't make it today, tomorrow for sure.

sentences.native: प्लान कैंसल हो गया, उसकी तबीयत ठीक नहीं है।
sentences.roman: plān kainsal ho gayā, uskī tabīyat ṭhīk nahīṃ hai.
sentences.en: The plan's off, she isn't well.

sentences.native: मैंने डिनर कैंसल कर दिया।
sentences.roman: maiṃne ḍinar kainsal kar diyā.
sentences.en: I cancelled the dinner.

sentences.native: चलो, पिक्चर अगले हफ़्ते पर टालते हैं।
sentences.roman: chalo, pikchar agle hafte par ṭālte haiṃ.
sentences.en: Let's push the film to next week.

sentences.native: बहाने मत बनाओ, सीधे बोलो कि तुम्हें नहीं आना।
sentences.roman: bahāne mat banāo, sīdhe bolo ki tumheṃ nahīṃ ānā.
sentences.en: Stop making excuses, just say you don't want to come.

sentences.native: कोई और दिन? इस वीकेंड मैं बिज़ी हूँ।
sentences.roman: koī aur din? is vīkeṇḍ maiṃ bizī hūṃ.
sentences.en: Some other day? I'm busy this weekend.

sentences.native: वो हमेशा आख़िरी मिनट पर प्लान कैंसल करता है।
sentences.roman: vo hameshā āxirī minaṭ par plān kainsal kartā hai.
sentences.en: He always cancels plans at the last minute.

sentences.native: देखते हैं, अगर टाइम मिला तो आऊँगा।
sentences.roman: dekhte haiṃ, agar ṭāim milā to āūṃgā.
sentences.en: We'll see, if I get time I'll come.

sentences.native: कोई बात नहीं, किसी और दिन मिलते हैं।
sentences.roman: koī bāt nahīṃ, kisī aur din milte haiṃ.
sentences.en: No problem, let's meet another day.
